1.title: The Beginning of the Gospel
1.themes: John the Baptist, Baptism of Jesus, Temptation, Calling Disciples, Miracles and Authority
1.outline:
I. John the Baptist Prepares the Way (1:1-8)
II. The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus (1:9-13)
III. Jesus Calls the First Disciples (1:14-20)
IV. Jesus Heals and Casts out Demons (1:21-45)
1.summary: The Gospel of Mark opens rapidly with the ministry of John the Baptist, followed by Jesus' baptism, temptation, and the launch of His public ministry in Galilee, marked by teaching with authority, calling disciples, and performing miraculous healings and exorcisms.

2.title: Jesus' Authority to Forgive Sins
2.themes: Forgiveness, Conflict with Religious Leaders, Fasting, Lord of the Sabbath
2.outline:
I. Jesus Forgives and Heals a Paralyzed Man (2:1-12)
II. Jesus Calls Levi and Eats with Sinners (2:13-17)
III. Questions About Fasting (2:18-22)
IV. Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath (2:23-28)
2.summary: Jesus demonstrates His divine authority to forgive sins by healing a paralyzed man, leading to rising opposition from religious leaders. Conflicts escalate over His association with sinners, His disciples' lack of fasting, and His interpretation of the Sabbath.

3.title: Appointing the Twelve Apostles
3.themes: Healing on the Sabbath, The Twelve Apostles, The Unforgivable Sin, Jesus' True Family
3.outline:
I. Healing a Man's Shriveled Hand on the Sabbath (3:1-6)
II. Crowds Follow Jesus (3:7-12)
III. Appointing the Twelve Apostles (3:13-19)
IV. Jesus Accused by His Family and Teachers of the Law (3:20-30)
V. Jesus' Mother and Brothers (3:31-35)
3.summary: Opposition intensifies after Jesus heals on the Sabbath. He selects twelve apostles to share in His ministry, faces accusations from religious leaders of being possessed by Beelzebul, and redefines His true family as those who do God's will.

4.title: Parables of the Kingdom
4.themes: The Parable of the Sower, The Purpose of Parables, Faith and Fear, Jesus' Power over Nature
4.outline:
I. The Parable of the Sower (4:1-20)
II. A Lamp on a Stand (4:21-25)
III. The Parable of the Growing Seed (4:26-29)
IV. The Parable of the Mustard Seed (4:30-34)
V. Jesus Calms the Storm (4:35-41)
4.summary: Jesus teaches the crowds through parables, focusing on the Parable of the Sower to illustrate the varied responses to the word of God. Later, He demonstrates His absolute authority over nature by calming a severe storm on the Sea of Galilee, astonishing His disciples.

5.title: Miracles of Healing and Restoration
5.themes: Demon Possession, Faith and Healing, Power over Death
5.outline:
I. Jesus Restores a Demon-Possessed Man (5:1-20)
II. Jesus Raises Jairus' Daughter and Heals a Bleeding Woman (5:21-43)
5.summary: Jesus continues to display His power by casting a legion of demons out of a man, healing a woman who had bled for twelve years simply through her faith-filled touch, and raising the young daughter of Jairus from the dead.

6.title: Rejection and Sending Out the Twelve
6.themes: Rejection at Nazareth, Sending the Apostles, Death of John the Baptist, Feeding the 5,000, Walking on Water
6.outline:
I. A Prophet Without Honor (6:1-6)
II. Jesus Sends Out the Twelve (6:7-13)
III. John the Baptist Beheaded (6:14-29)
IV. Jesus Feeds the Five Thousand (6:30-44)
V. Jesus Walks on the Water (6:45-56)
6.summary: Jesus faces rejection in His hometown of Nazareth. He commissions the Twelve for ministry. The tragic death of John the Baptist is recounted, followed by Jesus miraculously feeding five thousand people and walking on water, though the disciples struggle to understand.

7.title: Inner Purity and Ministry to Gentiles
7.themes: Tradition of the Elders, Inner Purity, Faith of Gentiles
7.outline:
I. That Which Defiles (7:1-23)
II. Jesus Honors a Syrophoenician Woman's Faith (7:24-30)
III. Jesus Heals a Deaf and Mute Man (7:31-37)
7.summary: Jesus confronts the Pharisees over their hypocritical reliance on human traditions regarding purity, teaching that defilement comes from the heart. He then ministers in Gentile territories, healing the daughter of a Syrophoenician woman and a deaf man.

8.title: Peter's Confession and the Cost of Discipleship
8.themes: Feeding the 4,000, The Yeast of the Pharisees, Peter's Confession, Prediction of the Passion
8.outline:
I. Jesus Feeds the Four Thousand (8:1-13)
II. The Yeast of the Pharisees and Herod (8:14-21)
III. Healing a Blind Man at Bethsaida (8:22-26)
IV. Peter Declares That Jesus is the Messiah (8:27-30)
V. Jesus Predicts His Death (8:31-38)
8.summary: After feeding four thousand, Jesus warns against the influence of the Pharisees. Peter explicitly confesses Jesus as the Messiah. Jesus then predicts His impending death and resurrection, teaching that true discipleship requires taking up one's cross.

9.title: The Transfiguration and True Greatness
9.themes: The Transfiguration, Healing a Boy with an Impure Spirit, Servant Leadership
9.outline:
I. The Transfiguration (9:1-13)
II. Jesus Heals a Boy Possessed by an Impure Spirit (9:14-29)
III. Jesus Predicts His Death a Second Time (9:30-32)
IV. Whoever is Not Against Us is For Us (9:33-41)
V. Causing to Stumble (9:42-50)
9.summary: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John, revealing His divine glory. Coming down the mountain, He heals a demon-possessed boy His disciples could not. He predicts His death again and redefines greatness as humble servanthood.

10.title: Teaching on Marriage, Wealth, and Servanthood
10.themes: Divorce, Little Children, The Rich Young Man, The Request of James and John, Healing Bartimaeus
10.outline:
I. Divorce (10:1-12)
II. The Little Children and Jesus (10:13-16)
III. The Rich and the Kingdom of God (10:17-31)
IV. Jesus Predicts His Death a Third Time (10:32-34)
V. The Request of James and John (10:35-45)
VI. Blind Bartimaeus Receives His Sight (10:46-52)
10.summary: Jesus teaches about the permanence of marriage, welcomes little children, and warns about the spiritual danger of wealth through the rich young ruler. He predicts His passion a third time, counters the disciples' ambition by modeling servanthood, and heals blind Bartimaeus.

11.title: The Triumphal Entry and Cleansing the Temple
11.themes: The Triumphal Entry, Cursing the Fig Tree, Cleansing the Temple, Authority of Jesus
11.outline:
I. Jesus Comes to Jerusalem as King (11:1-11)
II. Jesus Curses a Fig Tree and Clears the Temple Courts (11:12-19)
III. The Withered Fig Tree (11:20-26)
IV. The Authority of Jesus Questioned (11:27-33)
11.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem to shouts of 'Hosanna,' symbolically curses a barren fig tree, and drives the merchants out of the temple courts. His actions prompt the religious leaders to question His authority, which He brilliantly evades.

12.title: Controversies in Jerusalem
12.themes: Parable of the Tenants, Paying Taxes to Caesar, Marriage at the Resurrection, The Greatest Commandment, The Widow's Offering
12.outline:
I. The Parable of the Tenants (12:1-12)
II. Paying Taxes to Caesar (12:13-17)
III. Marriage at the Resurrection (12:18-27)
IV. The Greatest Commandment (12:28-34)
V. Whose Son Is the Messiah? (12:35-40)
VI. The Widow's Offering (12:41-44)
12.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the wicked tenants to indict the religious leaders. He navigates trap questions about taxes and the resurrection, identifies the greatest commandments as love for God and neighbor, and praises the sacrificial giving of a poor widow.

13.title: The Olivet Discourse
13.themes: Destruction of the Temple, Signs of the End of the Age, The Day and Hour Unknown
13.outline:
I. The Destruction of the Temple and Signs of the End Times (13:1-23)
II. The Return of the Son of Man (13:24-27)
III. The Day and Hour Unknown (13:28-37)
13.summary: Jesus predicts the total destruction of the temple and gives a prophetic discourse on the Mount of Olives regarding the signs of the end of the age, severe tribulations, the return of the Son of Man, and the urgent need for believers to remain watchful.

14.title: The Last Supper, Betrayal, and Arrest
14.themes: Anointing at Bethany, The Last Supper, Gethsemane, Betrayal, Peter's Denial
14.outline:
I. Jesus Anointed at Bethany (14:1-11)
II. The Lord's Supper (14:12-26)
III. Jesus Predicts Peter's Denial (14:27-31)
IV. Gethsemane (14:32-42)
V. Jesus Arrested (14:43-52)
VI. Jesus Before the Sanhedrin (14:53-65)
VII. Peter Disowns Jesus (14:66-72)
14.summary: The plot to kill Jesus unfolds as He is anointed for burial, celebrates the Last Supper, and agonizes in Gethsemane. Judas betrays Him, leading to His arrest and a late-night trial before the Sanhedrin, while Peter tragically denies knowing Him three times.

15.title: The Trial, Crucifixion, and Burial
15.themes: Trial Before Pilate, The Crucifixion, The Death of Jesus, The Burial
15.outline:
I. Jesus Before Pilate (15:1-15)
II. The Soldiers Mock Jesus (15:16-20)
III. The Crucifixion of Jesus (15:21-32)
IV. The Death of Jesus (15:33-41)
V. The Burial of Jesus (15:42-47)
15.summary: Jesus is tried by Pontius Pilate, who condemns Him to be crucified to placate the crowd. He is mocked by soldiers, crucified at Golgotha, and dies on the cross, after which Joseph of Arimathea boldly requests His body for a dignified burial.

16.title: The Resurrection
16.themes: The Empty Tomb, The Resurrection, Appearances of Jesus, The Great Commission
16.outline:
I. Jesus Has Risen (16:1-8)
II. Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene and Disciples (16:9-14)
III. The Great Commission and Ascension (16:15-20)
16.summary: Women visit the tomb on Sunday morning to find it empty and receive an angelic message that Jesus has risen. The ending recounts His appearances to His followers, the commissioning of the disciples to preach the gospel globally, and His ascension into heaven.
